\begin{tablenotes}[flushleft]
\footnotesize
\item \textit{Notes:} Each pair is one model fitted on HAR + calendar (\texttt{baseline}) and on all features,
with nothing else changed; the change is all features minus HAR + calendar on the same days. The per-bar linear
models are pre-tuned; on HAR + calendar all three take the OLS's position
on every day, so they share its Sharpe ratio. The tree rows summarise
45 pairs (every tuning configuration of the model set, 15 per estimator): the Sharpe
and $\Delta$Sharpe columns are medians, and each $t$ column gives the number of pairs with $t > 1.96$. The model-set
row covers the 51 pairs of the 112-forecast model set (the MinGRU is not in it): $\Delta$Sharpe mid
$> 0$ in 50 of 51, none significantly negative. Mid: the straddle is bought or sold at the 15:30 midpoint; crossed: a buy pays the ask and a sale receives the bid, the spread paid at entry only (settlement is cash at intrinsic). Sharpe ratio $=\sqrt{252}\,\bar r/\mathrm{sd}(r)$, annualised per trade day (the trade runs about 200 days a year). Every $t$ is Newey--West (Bartlett kernel, lag $\lfloor 1.5\,n^{1/3}\rfloor = 14$ at $n = 866$); the $t$ of a $\Delta$Sharpe is that of the mean daily return difference, so it tests the mean difference, not the Sharpe difference. Bold: $|t| > 1.96$ (5\,\%, two-sided), on the estimate and its $t$.
\end{tablenotes}
